items.text:
To refuse the absolute Fact is not to refuse reality, but to refuse the  tyranny  of  a  single,  unbiased  account.  The  past,  instead, becomes a field  of competing narratives, where truth is neither singular nor absolute. The vitality of history is not located in its occurrence  but  in  its  reconstruction;  it  is  the  historian, not the Event,  who  gives  shape  to  the  past.  This  radical displacement shifts  the weight from the occurrence to the observer, from the supposed  certainty  of  the  archive  to  the  dynamic  play  of perspectives within the narrative itself."
Graduate Level 28/07/2025 (Shift - 3)
- Q.195. "The view of history that we attempt to preserve is rigidly anchored on the document..."
What is the grammatical function of the clause "that we attempt to preserve"?

items.text: "Discourse analysis, the framework  through which society understands  truth,  is  based  on the assumption that power and knowledge are inextricably linked. Institutions take great pains to defend  this  order,  often  restricting validity to the concepts that the  dominant  culture  has  defined  as  rational.  When  history proceeds in this fashion, narratives tend to be linear, reinforcing the  established  hierarchy  rather  than  questioning  it.  Yet,  over time, subjugated knowledge-historical contents that have been buried or disguised-resurface. Initially, these counter-narratives are  dismissed  as  madness  or  as  deviations  to  be  corrected within  the  existing  disciplinary  structure.  However,  as  these voices  grow  in  volume  and  coherence,  they  begin to erode the legitimacy of the prevailing authority.

The evolution of such systems is not a straightforward process of liberation, as Enlightenment thinkers might argue, but rather a reorganization  of  how  power  operates.  Epistemic  shifts  occur when a new 'regime of truth' emerges-one that is not merely a reform  of  the  old  laws  but  a  fundamental  restructuring  of discipline. This change is not purely legal or moral; it involves a radical change in focus, akin to a microscopic realignment. The transition from public torture to the prison timetable,  for example,  did  not  merely  change  the  method  of  punishment;  it redefined the very target of control from the physical body to the soul."
Graduate Level 29/07/2025 (Shift - 3)

items.text: "It is with deep sorrow that we report a severe flood which, late on Tuesday night, destroyed the main bridge of Riverside Village. Although  the  rescue  teams  worked  tirelessly  in  the  dark,  the heavy  rain  caused  the  river  levels  to  rise, flooding many farms and  cellars.  Villagers  and  farmers  watched  helplessly  as  the bridge  was  swept  away.  Initial  reports  suggest  that  the  flood occurred because the drainage channels were blocked by debris, but experts are  currently  investigating  the  site.  The  Town Council  has  promised  a  complete  upgrade  of  the  drainage system to avoid such tragedies in coming years." Graduate Level 31/07/2025 (Shift - 3)

Epistemic  shifts  occur when a new 'regime of truth' emerges-one that is not merely a reform  of  the  old  laws  but  a  fundamental  restructuring  of discipline. This change is not purely legal or moral; it involves a radical change in focus, akin to a microscopic realignment. The transition from public torture to the prison timetable,  for example,  did  not  merely  change  the  method  of  punishment;  it redefined the very target of control from the physical body to the soul."
